functions.name: u32to8_little
functions.signature: static inline void u32to8_little(uint8_t *p, const uint32_t *w)
functions.description: Store a 32-bit word into 4 bytes in little-endian order. On platforms defined as little-endian (PYCRYPTO_LITTLE_ENDIAN), it memcpy’s for speed; otherwise it manually lays out bytes. Use to serialize a 32-bit value to a byte buffer in LE.
requirements: p must point to a writable buffer of at least 4 bytes.
w must point to a valid uint32_t.
This function performs no NULL checks; callers must ensure non-NULL pointers.
Endianness handling depends on compile-time macros (PYCRYPTO_LITTLE_ENDIAN).

functions.name: bytes_to_words
functions.signature: static inline int bytes_to_words(uint64_t *x, size_t words, const uint8_t *in, size_t len)
functions.description: Convert a big-endian byte string in[0..len-1] into a little-endian array of 64-bit words x[0..words-1]. Leading zero bytes are skipped; if the resulting number is zero, it returns success without writing nonzero words. The most significant bytes map to the highest-indexed word. Returns 0 on success or an ERR_* code from errors.h on failure.
requirements: x must point to an array of at least `words` uint64_t elements; the function zeroes all words.
in must point to at least `len` readable bytes; big-endian encoding is expected.
If `words == 0` or `len == 0`, the function returns ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_DATA (no conversion is performed).
If `x == NULL` or `in == NULL`, the function returns ERR_NULL.
If the number represented by `in` requires more than `words` 64-bit words, the function returns ERR_MAX_DATA and leaves `x` zeroed.
On success, returns 0 and writes the converted value into x in little-endian word order (least significant word at index 0).

functions.name: words_to_bytes
functions.signature: static inline int words_to_bytes(uint8_t *out, size_t len, const uint64_t *x, size_t words)
functions.description: Convert a little-endian array of 64-bit words x[0..words-1] into a big-endian byte string out[0..len-1], left-padded with zeros as needed. Trailing zero words (most significant) are ignored. Returns 0 on success or an ERR_* code from errors.h on failure.
requirements: out must point to a writable buffer of at least `len` bytes; the function zero-fills it before writing the number.
x must point to an array of at least `words` uint64_t elements containing the little-endian word representation (least significant word at index 0).
If `words == 0` or `len == 0`, the function returns ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_DATA.
If `x == NULL` or `out == NULL`, the function returns ERR_NULL.
If the non-zero value in `x` requires more than `len` bytes when encoded, the function returns ERR_MAX_DATA (no overflow occurs; the buffer remains zero-padded).
On success, returns 0 and writes the big-endian representation right-aligned within `len` bytes (left-padded with zeros).

functions.name: align_alloc
functions.signature: static inline void* align_alloc(size_t size, unsigned boundary)
functions.description: Allocate `size` bytes of memory aligned to `boundary` bytes. Uses the platform’s aligned allocation routine: _aligned_malloc (Windows), posix_memalign (POSIX), or memalign. Returns NULL on allocation failure or if the underlying API rejects the alignment.
requirements: boundary must satisfy the alignment constraints required by the platform API (commonly a power of two and a multiple of sizeof(void*)).
size may be zero or more; when zero, behavior follows the underlying API (may return NULL or a unique pointer).
The returned pointer must be freed with align_free (not free or _aligned_free directly) to ensure correct pairing across platforms.

functions.name: align_free
functions.description: Free memory previously allocated by align_alloc, dispatching to the matching platform-specific deallocator (_aligned_free, free). Safe to pass NULL (no effect).
requirements: mem must be either NULL or a pointer previously returned by align_alloc from the same library build; do not pass pointers from standard malloc/new.
Call exactly once per successful align_alloc to avoid leaks or double-free.

functions.name: memchr_not
functions.signature: static inline const uint8_t* memchr_not(const uint8_t* s, int c, size_t n)
functions.description: Scan the first n bytes of s and return a pointer to the first byte not equal to the value (unsigned char)c. Returns NULL if all n bytes equal c. Utility inverse of memchr for equality testing.
requirements: s must point to at least n readable bytes.
No NULL checks are performed; callers must pass a non-NULL pointer when n > 0.
c is interpreted as an unsigned byte value (0..255) when compared.

data_types.description: A buffer of exactly 4 bytes containing any byte values 0x00–0xFF. No encoding or structure is required. Used where functions load a 32-bit word from a 4-byte buffer in either little-endian or big-endian order.

A buffer of exactly 8 bytes containing any byte values 0x00–0xFF. No encoding or structure is required. Used where functions load a 64-bit word from an 8-byte buffer in either little-endian or big-endian order.

A byte string representing a non-negative integer encoded in big-endian (most significant byte first). Length may be zero or more bytes; leading zero bytes are allowed and may be skipped by parsers. Intended for conversion into arrays of little-endian 64-bit words.
A buffer of any length (including zero) containing unrestricted byte values 0x00–0xFF with no specific structure. Suitable for generic memory scanning or comparison operations.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary 4-byte buffer. Valid for both LE/BE loaders.
# Goal: Provide interesting, yet valid, 4-byte patterns that exercise edge cases
# and diverse values (e.g., zeros, all-ones, boundaries, alternating bits,
# ASCII-like, high-bit set, random). The fuzzer will resize to exactly 4 bytes,
# but we generate exactly 4 bytes here.

INTERESTING_WORDS: List[int] = [
    0x00000000,
    0xFFFFFFFF,
    0x00000001,
    0x80000000,
    0x7FFFFFFF,
    0x0000FFFF,
    0xFFFF0000,
    0x00FF00FF,
    0xFF00FF00,
    0x01020304,
    0x04030201,
    0x11223344,
    0xA5A5A5A5,
    0x5A5A5A5A,
    0xDEADBEEF,
    0xFEEDFACE,
    0xC0DEC0DE,
    0x13371337,
    0x00010000,
    0x00008000,
]

ASCII_WORDS: List[bytes] = [
    b"    ",      # spaces
    b"\x00\x00\x00\x00",
    b"\xff\xff\xff\xff",
    b"ABCD",
    b"0123",
    b"\n\r\t\x00",
    b"\x7f\x7f\x7f\x7f",
    b"\x80\x80\x80\x80",
]


def _random_word(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias toward interesting boundaries but allow wide coverage
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.55:
        return rng.choice(INTERESTING_WORDS)
    else:
        # Construct with biased bytes to hit 0x00/0xFF and mid values
        b0 = rng.choice([0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x7F, rng.randrange(256)])
        b1 = rng.choice([0x00, 0xFF, 0x01, 0xFE, rng.randrange(256)])
        b2 = rng.choice([0x00, 0xFF, 0x10, 0xEF, rng.randrange(256)])
        b3 = rng.choice([0x00, 0xFF, 0x20, 0xDF, rng.randrange(256)])
        return (b3 << 24) | (b2 << 16) | (b1 << 8) | b0


def _mix_endian(word: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Produce 4 bytes; fuzzer stubs treat as raw and interpret LE/BE in different targets.
    # Randomly choose representation styles to give different byte layouts.
    style = rng.randrange(5)
    if style == 0:
        # Native little-endian layout (common for LE loaders)
        return struct.pack('<I', word)
    elif style == 1:
        # Big-endian layout (common for BE loaders)
        return struct.pack('>I', word)
    elif style == 2:
        # Repeated single byte patterns (e.g., all-zero, all-FF)
        val = rng.choice([0x00, 0xFF, 0x7F, 0x80, word & 0xFF])
        return bytes([val]) * 4
    elif style == 3:
        # Alternating bit/byte patterns
        pattern = rng.choice([
            bytes([0xAA, 0x55, 0xAA, 0x55]),
            bytes([0x55, 0xAA, 0x55, 0xAA]),
            bytes([0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF]),
            bytes([0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00]),
        ])
        return pattern
    else:
        # ASCII-like buffers or control mixes
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            return rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS)
        # Compose mixed bytes from the word, shuffled
        b = list(struct.pack('>I', word))
        rng.shuffle(b)
        return bytes(b)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Sometimes directly return a chosen ASCII word to mix coverage
    if rng.random() < 0.20:
        return rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS)

    word = _random_word(rng)
    buf = _mix_endian(word, rng)

    # Ensure exactly 4 bytes (the fuzzer will also truncate/extend, but we aim to be exact)
    if len(buf) < 4:
        buf = (buf + b"\x00\x00\x00\x00")[:4]
    elif len(buf) > 4:
        buf = buf[:4]

    return buf

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces exactly 8 bytes of arbitrary binary data.
# It aims to cover edge and interesting 64-bit values when interpreted in
# both little-endian and big-endian loads used by the target stubs.

_INTERESTING_CONSTANTS: List[int] = [
    # All-zero / all-one
    0x0000000000000000,
    0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF,
    # Single-bit patterns
    0x0000000000000001,
    0x8000000000000000,
    0x0000000000000080,
    0x0000000000000100,
    # Boundary byte and word transitions
    0x00000000000000FF,
    0x000000000000FF00,
    0x0000000000FF0000,
    0x00000000FF000000,
    0x000000FF00000000,
    0x0000FF0000000000,
    0x00FF000000000000,
    0xFF00000000000000,
    # Alternating patterns
    0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA,
    0x5555555555555555,
    0xAAAAAAAA00000000,
    0x00000000AAAAAAAA,
    0x5555555500000000,
    0x0000000055555555,
    # Increasing/decreasing bytes
    0x0001020304050607,
    0x0706050403020100,
    # Sign-extension relevant values
    0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF,
    0x8000000000000001,
    # Mixed edge bytes
    0xFF00FF00FF00FF00,
    0x00FF00FF00FF00FF,
]

def _rand_bool(r: random.Random, p: float) -> bool:
    return r.random() < p

def _random_64(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Skew towards byte-patterned values while keeping randomness
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.6:
        # Build from bytes with bias towards {0x00,0xFF,0x01,0x80}
        bias = [0x00, 0xFF, 0x01, 0x80]
        val = 0
        for i in range(8):
            if _rand_bool(r, 0.6):
                b = r.choice(bias)
            else:
                b = r.randrange(0, 256)
            val |= (b & 0xFF) << (8 * (7 - i))
        return val
    elif choice < 0.9:
        # Random 64-bit
        return r.getrandbits(64)
    else:
        # Compose from 16-bit chunks with boundaries
        chunks = []
        bias16 = [0x0000, 0xFFFF, 0x00FF, 0xFF00, 0x8000, 0x7FFF, 0x0100, 0x0001]
        for _ in range(4):
            if _rand_bool(r, 0.7):
                chunks.append(r.choice(bias16))
            else:
                chunks.append(r.randrange(0, 1 << 16))
        val = 0
        for c in chunks:
            val = (val << 16) | (c & 0xFFFF)
        return val & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF

def _choose_value(r: random.Random) -> int:
    mode = r.randrange(0, 4)
    if mode == 0:
        return r.choice(_INTERESTING_CONSTANTS)
    elif mode == 1:
        # Neighbor around an interesting constant within few bits to test edge transitions
        base = r.choice(_INTERESTING_CONSTANTS)
        # Apply 1-3 random bit flips or +/- small deltas
        if _rand_bool(r, 0.5):
            flips = r.randint(1, 3)
            for _ in range(flips):
                base ^= 1 << r.randrange(0, 64)
            return base & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
        else:
            delta = r.randint(-255, 255)
            return (base + delta) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    elif mode == 2:
        return _random_64(r)
    else:
        # Construct value that is different when interpreted LE vs BE by arranging bytes
        # Mix low/high significance extremes
        low = r.choice([0x00, 0x01, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFF])
        high = r.choice([0x00, 0x01, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFF])
        mid_pattern = r.choice([
            [0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00],
            [0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF],
            [0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF],
            [0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00],
            [0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04, 0x05, 0x06],
            [0x06, 0x05, 0x04, 0x03, 0x02, 0x01],
        ])
        b = [high] + mid_pattern + [low]
        v = 0
        for x in b:
            v = (v << 8) | (x & 0xFF)
        return v

def _pack_bytes(v: int, le: bool) -> bytes:
    # Pack into bytes exactly 8 long in a chosen endianness to diversify FUZZ_PARAM_STR inputs
    if le:
        return struct.pack('<Q', v)
    else:
        return struct.pack('>Q', v)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    v = _choose_value(r)
    # Randomly decide layout to exercise both little- and big-endian paths in stubs
    le = _rand_bool(r, 0.5)
    data = _pack_bytes(v, le)

    # Optionally rotate or reverse bytes to create additional diversity while keeping validity
    transform = r.randrange(0, 4)
    b = bytearray(data)
    if transform == 1:
        # rotate left by k bytes
        k = r.randrange(0, 8)
        b = bytearray(b[k:] + b[:k])
    elif transform == 2:
        # rotate right by k bytes
        k = r.randrange(0, 8)
        b = bytearray(b[-k:] + b[:-k]) if k != 0 else b
    elif transform == 3:
        # reverse
        b.reverse()

    # Ensure length is exactly 8 bytes as required by the stubs
    return bytes(b[:8])

import random
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzzers that take arbitrary binary buffers (std::string)
# and exercise memchr_not(s, c, n). We want to generate interesting, yet valid
# byte sequences that cover edge cases:
# - Empty buffer
# - All-bytes equal to c
# - No byte equals c
# - First byte differs
# - Last byte differs
# - Alternating patterns around c
# - Long runs equal to c with a single differing byte at various positions
# - Random buffers with controlled probability of matching c
# - Full 0x00..0xFF sequences
# - Various lengths including boundaries (1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 255, 256, 1024)
# The fuzzer also provides an int c separately; we cannot set it directly here, but
# good initial corpus buffers should be useful across many values of c. We therefore
# embed multiple subcases concatenated, each prefixed with a small header that some
# fuzzers may split; but since FUZZ_PARAM_STR returns the whole buffer as-is, we
# simply provide a mixture of segments so that many properties hold for various c.
# Limit total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(length))

def _all_byte(value: int, length: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([value & 0xFF]) * length

def _sequence_range(start: int, step: int, length: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    v = start & 0xFF
    for _ in range(length):
        out.append(v)
        v = (v + step) & 0xFF
    return bytes(out)

def _alternating(a: int, b: int, length: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((a if (i % 2 == 0) else b) & 0xFF for i in range(length))

def _insert_single_diff(base: bytes, diff_byte: int, pos: int) -> bytes:
    if not base:
        return bytes([diff_byte & 0xFF])
    pos = max(0, min(pos, len(base) - 1))
    b = bytearray(base)
    b[pos] = diff_byte & 0xFF
    return bytes(b)

def _build_segments(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    segs: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Empty
    segs.append(b"")

    # 2) Small sizes around boundaries
    for ln in [1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32]:
        # random
        segs.append(_rand_bytes(rng, ln))
        # ascending sequence
        segs.append(_sequence_range(rng.randrange(256), 1, ln))
        # repeating single byte common values
        for v in [0x00, 0xFF, 0x20, 0x7F, 0x41, 0x61]:
            segs.append(_all_byte(v, ln))
        # alternating near-common values
        segs.append(_alternating(0x00, 0xFF, ln))
        segs.append(_alternating(0x20, 0x7F, ln))

    # 3) Longer runs with a single differing byte at various positions
    for ln in [17, 33, 64, 255, 256, 1024]:
        base_val = rng.randrange(256)
        base = _all_byte(base_val, ln)
        for pos in [0, ln // 2, ln - 1, rng.randrange(ln)]:
            diff = (base_val + rng.randrange(1, 255)) & 0xFF
            segs.append(_insert_single_diff(base, diff, pos))
        # also include the pure run (all equal)
        segs.append(base)
        # and the inverted: mostly non-base with a few equals
        buf = bytearray(_rand_bytes(rng, ln))
        for pos in [0, ln // 3, (2 * ln) // 3, ln - 1]:
            buf[pos] = base_val
        segs.append(bytes(buf))

    # 4) Full byte spectrum sequences
    full = bytes(range(256))
    segs.append(full)
    segs.append(full[::-1])
    # repeated spectrums shortened to fit
    segs.append((full * 3)[:600])

    # 5) Random buffers with controlled probability of a specific byte occurrence
    for ln in [5, 9, 17, 33, 65, 129, 257]:
        # choose a target byte and create buffer with varying densities
        t = rng.randrange(256)
        for pcent in [0, 5, 50, 95, 100]:
            buf = bytearray()
            for _ in range(ln):
                if rng.randrange(100) < pcent:
                    buf.append(t)
                else:
                    # pick a byte != t
                    v = rng.randrange(255)
                    if v >= t:
                        v += 1
                    buf.append(v)
            segs.append(bytes(buf))

    # 6) Crafted ends: first/last byte unique
    for ln in [10, 20, 40, 80]:
        fill = rng.randrange(256)
        # first differs
        segs.append(bytes([fill ^ 0xFF]) + _all_byte(fill, ln - 1))
        # last differs
        segs.append(_all_byte(fill, ln - 1) + bytes([fill ^ 0xAA]))

    return segs


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    segs = _build_segments(rng)

    # Shuffle segments to diversify early coverage regardless of truncation
    rng.shuffle(segs)

    # Concatenate until MAX_TOTAL limit
    out = bytearray()
    for seg in segs:
        if len(out) + len(seg) > MAX_TOTAL:
            # try to partially include a segment if beneficial
            remaining = MAX_TOTAL - len(out)
            if remaining <= 0:
                break
            if len(seg) == 0:
                continue
            out += seg[:remaining]
            break
        out += seg

    return bytes(out)
